analysis.title: October CPI increases risks of sequential hikes
key_insights: October core CPI rose 0.30% m/m, down from 0.33% in September but above the 0.2% consensus estimate. The three-month annualized core rate rose to roughly 3.7% from below 2.0% in August.

UBS says the report raises its conviction that the Fed has at least two more hikes to deliver. It also raises the risk of moving from gradual quarterly hikes to sequential 25bps hikes (e.g., December and January).
The CPI report carried no year-over-year calculation because of last year's government shutdown. UBS estimates core PCE is tracking from 3.1% to 3.3% y/y in October.

Core goods CPI eased to 0.16% m/m from 0.25%, but used cars fell 1.2% and masked strength elsewhere. Core goods excluding food, energy and used vehicles rose roughly 0.4%, up from an average of 0.1% m/m over the prior two months.
Tariff-sensitive categories rose: household furnishings +0.7%, toys +1.8%, appliances +1.3%. UBS reads this as consistent with lingering tariff pass-through.

The IT commodities group rose 0.4% m/m, extending gains across hardware items. These categories have small CPI weights but substantially larger PCE weights, so UBS expects AI-demand pressure to keep the Fed's concern elevated.
UBS says goods disinflation is becoming a less reliable theme going into 2027.
Shelter slowed to 0.30% from 0.39%. Owners' equivalent rent moderated to roughly 0.3% and primary rent to about 0.2%. The three-month OER trend is in the mid-3% annualized range, up from sub-3.0%.
Energy rose another 0.7% and added only about 5bp to headline CPI, a sharp fade from September's energy shock. Airfares rose 0.4%, a meaningful deceleration from September.

UBS expects the Fed to accelerate the pace of 25bp hikes rather than move to a 50bps hike. Governor Waller said a core CPI reading around 0.3% or higher could warrant considering a 50bps December hike, a threshold UBS says October effectively met. UBS still thinks FOMC support for 50bps is limited.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS sees limited FOMC support for a 50bps hike because it could signal policy is materially below its appropriate level and make the recalibration appear more open-ended. The expected path is gradual 25bps hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Governor Waller said core CPI around 0.3% or higher could warrant considering a 50bps December hike, a threshold October effectively met. UBS also sees a higher risk of consecutive 25bps hikes, such as December and January.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core CPI reading around 0.3% or higher, which Waller said could warrant a 50bps December hike. UBS says October effectively met this threshold.
